subject.title: Manage Claw cron jobs through the gateway

question: Should Claw removal fail closed when Gateway agent deletion is unavailable, or must the local fallback implement an equivalent durable cron-teardown contract?
rationale: Both choices define user-visible offline behavior and ownership of destructive recovery across the Gateway, scheduler, shared state, and local CLI; automation cannot safely select that permanent contract.

options.title: Require Gateway deletion
options.body: Fail Claw removal before local agent mutation whenever the Gateway cannot durably disable and record all agent-owned cron jobs.

options.title: Make fallback equivalent
options.body: Keep offline deletion only after adding the same durable cron discovery, teardown, retry, and recovery semantics to the local path.

options.title: Pause the cron slice
options.body: Hold this stacked PR until the RFC and canonical deletion lifecycle define a single accepted recovery contract.

recommendation.title: Require Gateway deletion
recommendation.body: Fail Claw removal before local agent mutation whenever the Gateway cannot durably disable and record all agent-owned cron jobs.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick has already reviewed and reproduced the exact deletion and recovery boundary at issue.
